items.title: Jack Kelly Interview, 1963-11-17
items.q: The interviewer mentions 'Derridge' in the context of a location ('plantation of? Derridge. Derridge. That's across the river.') and the interviewee does not respond with any personal connection or recognition of a person named Derridge.

ctx.x: Not very much. We're just about the same. He was about that height, right now. See, I'm five feet full. And he was there much longer. I couldn't say, he was five feet eight, five feet seven or eight. So, he wasn't much, you know, he was a stock. He was a stock I built there.

Mm-hmm. What were you telling us before we got the tape on about where he came from, the plantation of? Derridge. Derridge. That's across the river. That's on the other side. Oh. Yeah. And you were telling us about when Sheik and Howard came by for lessons. Do you remember them coming to the house?

Sheik used to come all the time and take lessons. My dad would try to learn different things about, you know, the expression and the feelings of music. You see, you don't just have to know music. Mm-hmm. You know, you have to play what you feel as well. Mm-hmm.
